abraham.title: Abraham serving the three angels (the Hospitality of Abraham), mosaic in Monreale Cathedral, Sicily
abraham.license: Public domain (PD-self: the photographer released the photo; the mosaic itself is centuries out of copyright)
abraham.note: Cropped to Abraham's head and upper body with the dish he brings (source 1086 x 1291, box x 600-930, y 400-812). Saved at native size, 330 x 412; the small copy is the same size, not upscaled. No public-domain colour scan of the San Vitale mosaic shows Abraham large enough (the only PD-Art scans crop him out or show him about 15px tall).

gideon.title: The Righteous Gideon, from the prophets tier of the iconostasis of the Dormition Cathedral, Kirillo-Belozersky Monastery
gideon.note: The Commons file shows three prophets (Micah, Elijah, Gideon); cropped to Gideon, the right-hand figure, head and shoulders (source 2100 x 839, box x 1398-1808, y 20-533). His scroll, outside the crop, begins with the word for fleece and names him. Saved at native size, 410 x 513.

peter.title: Saint Peter, encaustic icon at St Catherine's Monastery, Mount Sinai
peter.note: Taken from the 3840px Commons rendering of a 7792 x 13200 scan; cropped to the halo, face and shoulders, leaving out the three medallions at the top (box x 307-3379, y 1236-5076 of 3840 x 6505), then resized to 1120 x 1400.

ambrose.title: Saint Ambrose, mosaic in the Cappella Palatina, Palermo
ambrose.file: File:Unknown artist St Ambrose of Milan capella palatina palazzo dei normann a palermo palermo sicily italy circa 1140.jpg
ambrose.note: Cropped to the upper half of the standing figure, keeping the inscription SANCT AMBROSIVS (source 1000 x 2250, box x 0-1000, y 0-1250). Chosen because no large public-domain scan of the 5th-century San Vittore in Ciel d'Oro mosaic exists: the PD files are 138 and 312px wide, and the larger photos are CC BY or CC BY-SA.

john-cassian.title: St John Cassian, medallion in the Sacra Parallela manuscript, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Paris (Grec 923, folio 74v)
john-cassian.note: The Commons original, 250 x 267: the medallion cut from folio 74v, where the gold heading above it reads "of Abba Cassian" (ΤΟΥ ΑΒΒΑ ΚΑΣΣΙΑΝ). Gallica's scan of the whole folio (1349 x 1905) has no more detail. faces.py crops it inside the medallion's border, to the head and shoulders.
